whatItDoes: This is a browser explorable for Skyhook. It draws the EQ-5 peak-area taper and the EQ-6 two-arm mass ratio on one log axis across tip speeds of 0.5–4 km/s, with controls for derate, safety factor and fibre. Both quantities are functions of x = (v/V_c)·√(SF/(1−derate)), and they differ by exactly 2√π·x·erf(x): 6.05 at Rev A (taper 20.12, mass ratio 121.83×), crossing 1 at x = 0.5224, below which the taper is the larger. On every load the page re-derives all 14 mass-ratio and fibre-mass values in the rev_a.json snapshot from σ and ρ, and green badges appear only within 5e-4. It also re-derives six quoted figures from DECISION_LOG.md and glossary.md (the 440× is EQ-6 at 0 % derate, 440.3996; item 10's "~800× at SF 5" comes out at 484.06×). It refuses, saying what would help, when the canon file, a key or a fibre density is missing.
testsPin: The pins outside my own code are: (a) the 14 values in params/rev_a.json (40.32, 64.3, 121.83, 295.27, 3085.95 and their fibre tonnes, plus the 4 duplicates under the kinematics tier options), at the rel 5e-4 tolerance Skyhook's own test uses (tests/test_rev_a_physics.py:180-185), with the key parser checked against the file's actual key list; (b) the 3 rounded values (V_c_kms 2.73, specific_strength 3.72, tip_speed_to_Vc_ratio 0.92); (c) numbers parsed from the snapshotted docs: 440.3996 (DECISION_LOG.md:12), 23.64 % and SF 3.274 (:10, which reproduce only under "2 arms × EQ-5"), 8.2 and 20.1 (glossary.md:48); (d) CPython math.erf to 2e-15; (e) Skyhook's own physics/skyhook_physics.py (snapshot, run under python3 -I -B in a temp tree) agreeing with model.js to 1e-12 at 72 grid points, and its verify_rev_a() passing; (f) closed forms: the identity, Simpson quadrature of the constant-stress profile with no erf (1e-10), the crossover equation, and the small-x and large-x limits; (g) the program site's calculator lines :1135/:1158/:1159, quoted, checked verbatim against the checkout, and run in a vm sandbox (109×/55×/32×, 1,092/552/322 t). There are 18 unit tests plus 74 headless checks (ui-check.mjs: tiles against rev_a.json, snaps, keyboard, mouse drag, touch drag and tap at 390 px dark, refusals, canon withheld or σ-tampered or density-deleted over HTTP). Sabotage on a copy, as failing unit tests / failing ui checks: EQ-6 one arm 10/14; SF·(1−d) in x 11/12; EQ-4 without the 2 11/15; erf series off by one 12/16; EQ-5 as exp(x) 7/4, and the desktop pass stops early; badge tolerance 5e-2 1/3; ladder ignoring the speed in the key name 3/5; derate pct÷10 4/7, and the desktop pass stops early; gap with π for √π 4/2; no density from notes 1/2; "close" widened to 50 % 1/1; missing density falling back to a typed 1560 2/3. Several unit counts include the README test, which recomputes the README's numbers.

findingsAboutSourceRepo: All in Skyhook at 34935cb. (1) docs/DECISION_LOG.md:72 (item 10) says SF ≈ 5 takes the 2.5 km/s mass ratio "from ~41× to order ~800×". EQ-6 at SF 5 gives 484.06× at 0 % derate (like for like with ~41×, which is itself 40.32×), 1,104.53× at 15 % and 3,515.24× at 30 %. No ladder rung gives ~800×; 815× would need a 10 % derate, and that origin is a guess. At the conservative rung the SF 5 tether is 28.9× the SF 2.5 one. The bank's own BRIEFING.md repeats "~41× to ~800×". (2) tools/sims/skyhook_program_site.html:1089 and tools/sims/skyhook_calculator.jsx:279 label a one-arm ratio as "Tether ÷ payload mass" (mr at :1159; jsx :112-113, whose comment says "per arm"), while rev_a.json's ratio is two-arm. Measured headless at the site's defaults: Conservative 109× / 1,092 t, Baseline 55× / 552 t, Optimistic 32× / 322 t, against canon 121.83× / 609.1 t, 64.30× / 321.5 t, 40.32× / 201.6 t. (3) DEVIATIONS item 8, quantified: the site's d = 0.6/0.72/0.85 (:1135; same ladder in calculator.jsx:20-22) are 40/28/15 % derates. Its Conservative tonnage is 1.79× the canon's, and its "Optimistic" rung is the canon's baseline derate. (4) skyhook_program_site.html:1179 flags x = v·√SF/V_c,derated > 1.35 as "bad". The canon's guardrail is v_tip/V_c ≤ 1.3 (params/rev_a.json:98; docs/project_instructions.md:74), a different quantity, so the site marks its own Rev A reference red in all three modes (x = 1.871/1.708/1.572, measured). (5) docs/verification_memo.md:14 and :43 record SK99 as corrected to 3.6 GPa "in the site, calculator, and instructions", but calculator.jsx:11 still has sigma 3.9e9. (6) params/rev_a.json cannot feed EQ-4 for its own alternative fibres: Dyneema_SK99_GPa (:71) has no density anywhere in the file, and T1100G's density exists only inside the prose of _t1100g_note (:74). The 0 % and 15 % derates exist only in key names (:85, :87) and in the _derate_note prose (:68). (7) Cosmetic: glossary.md:48, DECISION_LOG.md:20 and the taper_ratio docstring at physics/skyhook_physics.py:214 state V_c = 2.73, and at that value the taper evaluates to 8.14 (8.1), or 19.99 (20.0) with the derate. The quoted 8.2 and 20.1 need V_c = 2.7269 from σ and ρ. materials.V_c_kms 2.73 (:64) misses every ladder rung by 0.61–1.45 % if used as an input. (8) Observation, not a defect: tests/test_rev_a_physics.py:156-162 (EQ-6 > EQ-5) holds at the reference but is false below x = 0.5224, and it compares EQ-6 at 30 % derate with EQ-5 at none.
deviationsFromProposal: (1) I dropped the proposal's test "EQ-6 > EQ-5 for every grid point in the slider ranges" because it is false. Mass ÷ taper = 2√π·x·erf(x) crosses 1 at x = 0.5224, and the sliders reach x = 0.18 (0.5 km/s, SF 1, 0 %: mass ratio 0.138, taper 1.034). The page marks the crossing and a test pins the opposite claim. (2) The proposal's "Vc(3.6 GPa, 970) = 2.72" is not computable from canon: rev_a.json has no SK99 density (970 is only in docs/project_instructions.md:67). The page refuses SK99 with what would help; a custom fibre, marked not canon and drawn dashed, lets a reader type 970. (3) T1100G's density is read out of the prose of _t1100g_note with a strict pattern, and the page says so. (4) I did not draw the "2 % guardrail": that 2 % is verify_rev_a's tolerance and the tests' TOL, not a design limit in rev_a.json. The 1.3 guardrail is drawn as v_tip/V_c, as in the file's _ratio_note. (5) erf uses the all-positive series (A&S 7.1.6, matching CPython to 2e-15) instead of A&S 7.1.26; the tests still check that 7.1.26 is within its stated 1.5e-7. (6) The derated taper is stated explicitly as EQ-5 at the same x as EQ-6 (the glossary's 20.1 convention), with the no-derate taper_ratio() value shown beside it. (7) Custom-fibre curves use the same two hues, dashed, with a "not canon" chip, rather than a different colour, so colour stays tied to the quantity. (8) Additions: the cross-section profile chart (taper = peak height, mass = 2 × 2x² × mean height); a quoted-history panel with six verbatim quotes and verdicts, which is where the item 10 finding came from; an oracle test against Skyhook's own skyhook_physics.py; a test that runs the program site's calculator lines verbatim; and the rounded-V_c and tamper tests.
notBuilt: (1) The page reads a snapshot, not params/rev_a.json live. Landing needs the twin's loadRevA() in tools/twin/params-loader.js, which needs the repo served over HTTP. (2) The badge assertions were not ported into Skyhook's tests/test_rev_a_physics.py, and pytest is not installed here; the snapshotted physics module was run directly as an oracle instead. (3) SK99 cannot be shown from canon at all: it is refused for want of a density. (4) The model is the canon's single-material constant-stress tether (whole tether as Zylon, no gravity gradient or orbit), not the Spectra-core/Zylon-outer construction baseline. (5) The physical derivation of the profile is my own, from the constant-stress taper; I have not read Moravec 1977 or the Forward source. The A&S equation number 7.1.6 is from memory. (6) The origin of "~800×" is undetermined. (7) No person from the program has used the page. (8) Under two sabotages a ui-check section stops at its first missing element, so those ui counts are lower bounds. It has not passed Skyhook's Rule 1 canon review, a verification memo or the pytest suite.
